## Summary

Sentry issue `NUKE-PROD-CV` is a real bug in `bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent` at `main.go:241`, filed automatically by the sentry-fix-agent from the High/High real bug deep verdict — that verdict is the approval gate, so this spec is approved rather than drafted.

## Problem

exitErrorForStatus (main.go:241) returns an error when the agent publishes Status=failed — deliberately forcing exit 1 — but the error carries only status and phase, not result.Message, so eight distinct planning failure modes collapse into one cause-less Sentry issue.

## Reproduction

The implicated source location from the deep verdict is `main.go:241` in `bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent` (resolution rule: `candidate position 1 (bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent)`), Sentry issue `NUKE-PROD-CV`.

## Recommended Fix

In finishRun, attach result.Message (truncated), task_id, task_type and phase to ctx via errors.AddToContext before exitErrorForStatus returns, so Sentry tags carry the cause without changing grouping; optionally exclude expected business-rule planning failures via a service.OptionsFn ExcludeErrors predicate while keeping the non-zero exit.

1	// Copyright (c) 2026 Benjamin Borbe All rights reserved.
2	// Use of this source code is governed by a BSD-style

4	
5	// Command github-dark-factory-agent is the canonical AI-heavy agent: one Claude
6	// invocation per phase, all logic in the prompt + allowed tools.
7	//
8	// This binary is the Kafka entry point — spawned as a K8s Job by
9	// task/executor with TASK_CONTENT + TASK_ID + PHASE + KAFKA_BROKERS env.
10	// For local CLI mode (file-based), see cmd/run-task/main.go.
11	//
12	// Reference implementation for AI-heavy agents using the agent framework
13	// (lib.NewAgent + claude.NewAgentStep). Other agents (trade-analysis,
14	// pr-reviewer) follow the same shape — copy this main.go and swap
15	// prompts/tools.
16	package main
17	
18	import (
19		"context"
20		"os"
21		"strings"
22		"time"
23	
24		agentlib "github.com/bborbe/agent"
25		claudelib "github.com/bborbe/agent/claude"
26		delivery "github.com/bborbe/agent/delivery"
27		"github.com/bborbe/agent/envparse"
28		libmetrics "github.com/bborbe/agent/metrics"
29		"github.com/bborbe/cqrs/base"
30		"github.com/bborbe/errors"
31		libkafka "github.com/bborbe/kafka"
32		githubapp "github.com/bborbe/maintainer/githubapp"
33		libsentry "github.com/bborbe/sentry"
34		"github.com/bborbe/service"
35		libtime "github.com/bborbe/time"
36		"github.com/bborbe/vault-cli/pkg/domain"
37		sentry "github.com/getsentry/sentry-go"
38		"github.com/golang/glog"
39		"github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus"
40		"github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/push"
41	
42		"github.com/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent/pkg/factory"
43		"github.com/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent/pkg/githubauth"
44	)
45	
46	// agentName is the identity string used for Prometheus metric grouping and logging.
47	const agentName = "github-dark-factory-agent"
48	
49	const (
50		// statusMessageMaxRunes bounds the Result.Message copied into the
51		// non-zero-exit error (and therefore into the pod log and the Sentry
52		// event value). A failed ai_review result can carry a long rationale.
53		statusMessageMaxRunes = 500
54	
55		// causePrefixMaxRunes bounds the cause component of the Sentry
56		// fingerprint so unrelated failures stay in separate issues without
57		// turning every distinct message into its own issue.
58		causePrefixMaxRunes = 100
59	)
60	
61	// truncateRunes returns s capped at max runes plus a trailing ellipsis. It
62	// counts runes, not bytes, so a multi-byte message is never cut mid-rune.
63	func truncateRunes(s string, max int) string {
64		if max < 0 {
65			return ""
66		}
67		runes := []rune(s)
68		if len(runes) <= max {
69			return s
70		}
71		return string(runes[:max]) + "..."
72	}
73	
74	// causePrefix returns a bounded, stable grouping key derived from
75	// Result.Message: the first line, trimmed, capped at causePrefixMaxRunes.
76	// An empty message yields "unknown" so the fingerprint is never empty.
77	func causePrefix(message string) string {
78		line := message
79		if idx := strings.IndexByte(line, '\n'); idx >= 0 {
80			line = line[:idx]
81		}
82		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
83		if line == "" {
84			return "unknown"
85		}
86		return truncateRunes(line, causePrefixMaxRunes)
87	}
88	
89	func main() {
90		sentry.AddGlobalEventProcessor(sentryFingerprintProcessor)
91		app := &application{}
92		os.Exit(service.Main(context.Background(), app, &app.SentryDSN, &app.SentryProxy))
93	}
94	
95	type application struct {
96		SentryDSN   string `required:"false" arg:"sentry-dsn"   env:"SENTRY_DSN"   usage:"SentryDSN"    display:"length"`
97		SentryProxy string `required:"false" arg:"sentry-proxy" env:"SENTRY_PROXY" usage:"Sentry Proxy" display:"length"`
98	
99		// Claude Code CLI configuration
100		ClaudeConfigDir claudelib.ClaudeConfigDir `required:"false" arg:"claude-config-dir" env:"CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR" usage:"Claude Code config directory"`
101	
102		// Agent directory (contains .claude/ with CLAUDE.md and commands)
103		AgentDir claudelib.AgentDir `required:"false" arg:"agent-dir" env:"AGENT_DIR" usage:"Agent directory with .claude/ config" default:"agent"`
104	
105		// Allowed tools (comma-separated)
106		AllowedToolsRaw string `required:"false" arg:"allowed-tools" env:"ALLOWED_TOOLS" usage:"Comma-separated list of allowed tools"`
107	
108		// Task content from agent pipeline
109		TaskContent string `required:"true" arg:"task-content" env:"TASK_CONTENT" usage:"Raw task markdown from vault"`
110	
111		// Environment context passed to prompt (comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs)
112		EnvContextRaw string `required:"false" arg:"env-context" env:"ENV_CONTEXT" usage:"Comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs for prompt context"`
113	
114		// Environment variables passed to Claude CLI process (comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs).
115		// Use this for ad-hoc / less-common env vars. The three load-bearing Anthropic provider
116		// vars below have dedicated arg slots so they don't have to be packed into this string.
117		ClaudeEnvRaw string `required:"false" arg:"claude-env" env:"CLAUDE_ENV" usage:"Comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs for Claude CLI environment"`
118	
119		// Anthropic-compatible provider routing. Setting AnthropicBaseURL + AnthropicAuthToken
120		// routes the claude CLI to an alt-provider (e.g. MiniMax via https://api.minimax.io/anthropic).
121		// AnthropicModel drives both the `--model` CLI flag and the ANTHROPIC_MODEL env var seen by
122		// the claude subprocess. Non-empty values override the same keys in ClaudeEnvRaw.
123		AnthropicBaseURL   string                `required:"false" arg:"anthropic-base-url"   env:"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"   usage:"Anthropic-compatible API base URL"`
124		AnthropicAuthToken string                `required:"false" arg:"anthropic-auth-token" env:"ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN" usage:"Bearer token for ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"                                  display:"length"`
125		AnthropicModel     claudelib.ClaudeModel `required:"false" arg:"anthropic-model"      env:"ANTHROPIC_MODEL"      usage:"Model name; also exposed to the claude subprocess as ANTHROPIC_MODEL"                  default:"sonnet"`
126	
127		// Branch for Kafka result delivery
128		Branch base.Branch `required:"false" arg:"branch" env:"BRANCH" usage:"branch"`
129	
130		// TopicPrefix is an explicit Kafka topic prefix, independent of Branch.
131		TopicPrefix base.TopicPrefix `required:"false" arg:"topic-prefix" env:"TOPIC_PREFIX" usage:"Explicit Kafka topic prefix; empty means unprefixed topics"`
132	
133		// Phase to run (framework requires explicit phase)
134		Phase domain.TaskPhase `required:"false" arg:"phase" env:"PHASE" usage:"Agent phase: planning | execution | ai_review" default:"execution"`
135	
136		// GitHub token for authenticated clones + REST API calls (planning phase).
137		// Used as the raw fallback credential when GitHub App creds are absent
138		// (local cmd/run-task path where the operator exports `gh auth token`).
139		GhToken string `required:"false" arg:"gh-token" env:"GH_TOKEN" usage:"GitHub token for clone + PR inspection (raw fallback when App creds unset)" display:"length"`
140	
141		// GitHub App authentication. When APP_ID, INSTALLATION_ID, and a PEM (file
142		// or inline) are all set, the pod mints a short-lived installation access
143		// token at startup and forwards it to every git/gh subprocess as GH_TOKEN.
144		// The cluster pod sets these (GH_TOKEN is empty there); locally they are
145		// absent and the agent falls back to the raw GhToken above.
146		AppID          int64  `required:"false" arg:"app-id"          env:"APP_ID"          usage:"GitHub App ID (numeric); enables App auth when set with INSTALLATION_ID + PEM"`
147		InstallationID int64  `required:"false" arg:"installation-id" env:"INSTALLATION_ID" usage:"GitHub App Installation ID (numeric)"`
148		PEMKeyFile     string `required:"false" arg:"pem-key-file"    env:"PEM_KEY_FILE"    usage:"Path to the GitHub App private key (PEM file mounted from k8s Secret)"`
149		PEMKey         string `required:"false" arg:"pem-key"         env:"PEM_KEY"         usage:"GitHub App private key (PEM) as env var content; mutually exclusive with PEM_KEY_FILE" display:"length"`
150	
151		// Workdir paths for bare-clone cache and per-task worktrees.
152		ReposPath string `required:"false" arg:"repos-path" env:"REPOS_PATH" usage:"Root path for bare-clone cache"   default:"/repos"`
153		WorkPath  string `required:"false" arg:"work-path"  env:"WORK_PATH"  usage:"Root path for per-task worktrees" default:"/work"`
154	
155		// Kafka delivery (optional — only active when TASK_ID is set)
156		KafkaBrokers libkafka.Brokers        `required:"false" arg:"kafka-brokers" env:"KAFKA_BROKERS" usage:"Comma separated list of Kafka brokers"`
157		TaskID       agentlib.TaskIdentifier `required:"false" arg:"task-id"       env:"TASK_ID"       usage:"Agent task identifier for publishing results back to task controller"`
158	
159		PushgatewayURL string `required:"false" arg:"pushgateway-url" env:"PUSHGATEWAY_URL" usage:"Prometheus PushGateway URL"          default:"http://pushgateway:9090"`
160		TaskType       string `required:"false" arg:"task-type"       env:"TASK_TYPE"       usage:"Task type label for metric grouping" default:"unknown"`
161	}
162	
163	func (a *application) Run(ctx context.Context, _ libsentry.Client) error {
164		registry := prometheus.NewRegistry()
165		jobMetrics := libmetrics.NewJobMetrics(registry, libtime.NewCurrentDateTime())
166		pusher := push.New(a.PushgatewayURL, libmetrics.BuildJobMetricsName(agentName)).
167			Grouping("agent", agentName).
168			Grouping("task_type", a.TaskType).
169			Collector(registry)
170		defer func() {
171			if err := pusher.PushContext(ctx); err != nil {
172				glog.Warningf("prometheus push failed: %v", err)
173				return
174			}
175			glog.V(2).Infof("prometheus push completed")
176		}()
177		start := libtime.NewCurrentDateTime().Now().Time()
178	
179		glog.V(2).Infof("github-dark-factory-agent started phase=%s", a.Phase)
180	
181		// Resolve the GitHub credential (App IAT or raw GH_TOKEN fallback) and make
182		// it usable by every git/gh subprocess. See prepareAuth.
183		resolvedToken, err := a.prepareAuth(ctx)
184		if err != nil {
185			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
186			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
187			return err
188		}
189	
190		deliverer := delivery.NewNoopResultDeliverer()
191		if a.TaskID != "" {
192			if len(a.KafkaBrokers) == 0 {
193				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
194				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
195				return errors.Errorf(ctx, "KAFKA_BROKERS must be set when TASK_ID is set")
196			}
197			syncProducer, err := factory.CreateSyncProducer(ctx, a.KafkaBrokers)
198			if err != nil {
199				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
200				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
201				return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "create sync producer")
202			}
203			defer func() {
204				if err := syncProducer.Close(); err != nil {
205					glog.Warningf("close sync producer failed: %v", err)
206				}
207			}()
208			deliverer = factory.CreateKafkaResultDeliverer(
209				syncProducer, a.TopicPrefix, a.TaskID, a.TaskContent,
210				libtime.NewCurrentDateTime(),
211			)
212		}
213	
214		claudeEnv := a.buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken)
215	
216		repoManager := factory.CreateRepoManager(a.ReposPath, a.WorkPath, resolvedToken)
217		githubClient := factory.CreateGitHubClient(resolvedToken)
218		claudeProber := factory.CreateClaudeProber(a.ClaudeConfigDir)
219		provider := factory.CreateAgentProvider(
220			a.ClaudeConfigDir,
221			a.AgentDir,
222			a.AnthropicModel,
223			resolvedToken,
224			claudeEnv,
225			repoManager,
226			githubClient,
227			claudeProber,
228			// Re-mint before the push: the installation token is minted once here at
229			// startup and expires after 60 minutes, but a lifecycle run routinely
230			// takes longer, so the final push would be refused as an invalid token.
231			a.resolveAuth,
232		)
233		agent, err := provider.Get(ctx, agentlib.TaskType(a.TaskType))
234		if err != nil {
235			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
236			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
237			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "select agent for task_type")
238		}

251	// finishRun publishes the agent's result and then decides the Job's exit code.
252	// It exists as one call so Run stays within its funlen budget.
253	func finishRun(
254		ctx context.Context,
255		result *agentlib.Result,
256		phase domain.TaskPhase,
257	) error {
258		if err := agentlib.PrintResult(ctx, result); err != nil {
259			return err
260		}
261		return exitErrorForStatus(ctx, result.Status, phase, result.Message)
262	}
263	
264	// exitErrorForStatus returns a non-nil error when the agent's published status
265	// must fail the Job, and nil when the Job may exit 0.
266	//
267	// A failed result is still published to the task, but the Job must also exit
268	// non-zero. The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded
269	// in agent-task-executor's job_watcher), so returning nil here makes a failed run
270	// indistinguishable from a completed one: the failure is written as a phase
271	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at human_review
272	// as though a human had parked it deliberately (2026-11-03, task ceb79961: a Job
273	// that published Status=failed for a git clone error exited 0 and parked the
274	// task).
275	//
276	// needs_input is deliberately NOT a failure: parking for a human answer is that
277	// status's intent, and it reaches the same park path on purpose.
278	func exitErrorForStatus(
279		ctx context.Context,
280		status agentlib.AgentStatus,
281		phase domain.TaskPhase,
282		message string,
283	) error {
284		if status != agentlib.AgentStatusFailed {
285			return nil
286		}
287		displayMessage := truncateRunes(message, statusMessageMaxRunes)
288		if displayMessage == "" {
289			displayMessage = "(no message)"
290		}
291		err := errors.Errorf(
292			ctx,
293			"agent reported status %q for phase %q: %s",
294			status,
295			phase,
296			displayMessage,
297		)
298		return &statusError{
299			err: err,
300			fingerprint: []string{
301				"agent-status-failed",
302				string(phase),
303				causePrefix(message),
304			},
305		}
306	}
307	
308	// fingerprinter is implemented by errors that know their Sentry grouping key.
309	type fingerprinter interface {
310		Fingerprint() []string
311	}
312	
313	// statusError is the non-zero-exit error for a failed agent result. The
314	// capture-site stack is identical for every failure, so Sentry would merge
315	// unrelated planning / execution / ai_review causes into one issue; this type
316	// carries an explicit fingerprint (phase + bounded cause prefix) that
317	// sentryFingerprintProcessor installs on the event.
318	type statusError struct {
319		err         error
320		fingerprint []string
321	}
322	
323	func (e *statusError) Error() string { return e.err.Error() }
324	
325	// Unwrap keeps errors.Is / errors.As working through the wrapper.
326	func (e *statusError) Unwrap() error { return e.err }
327	
328	// Cause keeps github.com/bborbe/errors DataFromError traversal working.
329	func (e *statusError) Cause() error { return e.err }
330	
331	// Fingerprint is the Sentry grouping key for this failure.
332	func (e *statusError) Fingerprint() []string { return e.fingerprint }
333	
334	// sentryFingerprintProcessor installs the fingerprint carried by a
335	// fingerprinter error onto the Sentry event. It is a no-op for every other
336	// error, so it can be registered globally: service.Main owns the Sentry client
337	// and exposes no per-client event-processor hook.
338	func sentryFingerprintProcessor(
339		event *sentry.Event,
340		hint *sentry.EventHint,
341	) *sentry.Event {
342		if event == nil || hint == nil || hint.OriginalException == nil {
343			return event
344		}
345		var f fingerprinter
346		if errors.As(hint.OriginalException, &f) {
347			event.Fingerprint = f.Fingerprint()
348		}
349		return event
350	}

352	// buildClaudeEnv assembles the Claude CLI subprocess env from the raw env
353	// pairs plus the Anthropic provider-routing overrides. resolvedToken, when
354	// non-empty, is threaded in as GH_TOKEN — the ai_review phase's Claude
355	// subprocess shells `gh pr view/diff`, and the runner strips pod env to an
356	// allowlist, so the token must be passed explicitly (os.Setenv in prepareAuth
357	// covers the dark-factory daemon path, not the Claude runner).
358	func (a *application) buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken string) map[string]string {
359		claudeEnv := envparse.KeyValuePairs(a.ClaudeEnvRaw)
360		if claudeEnv == nil {
361			claudeEnv = map[string]string{}
362		}
363		if a.AnthropicBaseURL != "" {
364			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"] = a.AnthropicBaseURL

366		if a.AnthropicAuthToken != "" {

378	// prepareAuth resolves the GitHub credential and makes it usable by every
379	// git/gh subprocess: it exports GH_TOKEN (covering the dark-factory daemon,
380	// which inherits os.Environ() for its `git push`) and installs git's credential
381	// helper via `gh auth setup-git`. Returns the resolved token for the
382	// RepoManager / GitHub client / gh-token preflight wiring.
383	func (a *application) prepareAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
384		resolvedToken, err := a.resolveAuth(ctx)
385		if err != nil {
386			return "", err
387		}
388		// resolvedToken is always non-empty here (resolveAuth errors otherwise), but
389		// guard defensively — an empty GH_TOKEN would mislead the daemon subprocess.
390		if resolvedToken != "" {
391			if err := os.Setenv("GH_TOKEN", resolvedToken); err != nil {
392				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "export GH_TOKEN")
393			}
394		}
395		if err := githubauth.NewGhAuthSetupGit(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
396			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "gh auth setup-git")
397		}
398		// A file the daemon re-reads outlives the token bound into gh's helper: the
399		// installation token expires after 60 minutes and the lifecycle daemon keeps
400		// its startup environment, so a long run's own `git fetch` would use a dead
401		// token (2026-11-03, bborbe/trading#433).
402		if err := githubauth.NewFileBackedHelper(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
403			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "configure file-backed credential helper")
404		}
405		return resolvedToken, nil
406	}

408	// resolveAuth resolves the GitHub credential forwarded to every git/gh
409	// subprocess. It prefers GitHub App authentication: when APP_ID,
410	// INSTALLATION_ID, and a PEM (file or inline) are all set, it mints a
411	// short-lived installation access token via githubapp.MintIAT. Otherwise it
412	// falls back to the raw GH_TOKEN input — the local cmd/run-task path where the
413	// operator exports `gh auth token`. When neither is configured it returns a
414	// clear error, since the agent cannot clone or push without a credential.
415	//
416	// The token is a runtime value (not a config input), so it is returned to the
417	// caller rather than stored on the argument-parsed application struct —
418	// argument/v2 panics when reflecting over unexported struct fields at startup.
419	func (a *application) resolveAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
420		hasPEMFile := a.PEMKeyFile != ""
421		hasPEMContent := a.PEMKey != ""
422		useGitHubApp := a.AppID != 0 && a.InstallationID != 0 && (hasPEMFile || hasPEMContent)
423		if useGitHubApp {
424			appCfg := githubapp.Config{AppID: a.AppID, InstallationID: a.InstallationID}
425			if hasPEMFile {
426				appCfg.PEMPath = a.PEMKeyFile
427			} else {
428				appCfg.PEM = []byte(a.PEMKey)
429			}
430			// Startup auth must not be killed by the task's work deadline: mint on a
431			// fresh bounded context (keeps ctx values, drops the caller's
432			// deadline/cancel) so a near-deadline task can't fail the token mint.
433			mintCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 30*time.Second)
434			defer cancel()
435			iat, err := githubapp.MintIAT(mintCtx, appCfg)
436			if err != nil {
437				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "mint github app iat")
438			}
439			glog.V(2).Infof(
440				"github-dark-factory-agent auth mode=github-app app_id=%d installation_id=%d",
441				a.AppID, a.InstallationID,
442			)
443			return iat, nil
444		}
445		if a.GhToken != "" {
446			glog.V(2).Infof("github-dark-factory-agent auth mode=gh-token (raw GH_TOKEN fallback)")
447			return a.GhToken, nil
448		}
449		return "", errors.Errorf(
450			ctx,
451			"github-dark-factory-agent auth: no credentials configured — set GitHub App creds (APP_ID, INSTALLATION_ID, PEM_KEY_FILE or PEM_KEY) or GH_TOKEN",
452		)
453	}

23	// TestExitErrorForStatus guards the exit-code contract between this agent and
24	// the executor that watches its Job.
25	//
26	// The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded in
27	// agent-task-executor's job_watcher) and never reads the Status this agent
28	// publishes. So a run that reports failure but exits 0 is written as a phase
29	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at
30	// human_review as though a human had parked it deliberately.
31	//
32	// Observed 2026-11-03: task ceb79961 published Status=failed for
33	// "git clone --bare: Failed to connect to github.com port 443", exited 0, and
34	// parked at human_review.
35	func TestExitErrorForStatus(t *testing.T) {
36		ctx := context.Background()
37		phase := domain.TaskPhase("execution")
38	
39		cases := []struct {
40			name    string
41			status  agentlib.AgentStatus
42			message string
43			wantErr bool
44		}{
45			{
46				name:    "failed must fail the Job so the executor does not record a phase success",
47				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusFailed,
48				message: "execution: ensure worktree: clone boom",
49				wantErr: true,
50			},
51			{
52				name:    "done exits 0",
53				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusDone,
54				wantErr: false,
55			},
56			{
57				name:    "in_progress exits 0",
58				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusInProgress,
59				wantErr: false,
60			},
61			{
62				// needs_input reaches the same park path on purpose: the task is meant
63				// to wait at human_review for an answer, not to be re-driven.
64				name:    "needs_input exits 0 — parking for a human answer is its intent",
65				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusNeedsInput,
66				wantErr: false,
67			},
68		}
69	
70		for _, c := range cases {
71			t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
72				err := exitErrorForStatus(ctx, c.status, phase, c.message)
73				if c.wantErr && err == nil {
74					t.Fatalf(
75						"status %q: expected a non-nil error, got nil — the Job would exit 0 and the executor would record it as a phase success",
76						c.status,
77					)
78				}
79				if !c.wantErr && err != nil {
80					t.Fatalf("status %q: expected nil, got %v", c.status, err)
81				}
82				if c.wantErr && !strings.Contains(err.Error(), c.message) {
83					t.Fatalf(
84						"failed error must include Result.Message %q, got %q",
85						c.message,
86						err.Error(),
87					)
88				}
89			})
90		}
91	}

147	// truncateRunes returns s capped at max runes plus a trailing ellipsis. It
148	// counts runes, not bytes, so a multi-byte message is never cut mid-rune.
149	func truncateRunes(s string, max int) string {
150		if max < 0 {

1	// Copyright (c) 2025 Benjamin Borbe All rights reserved.
2	// Use of this source code is governed by a BSD-style
3	// license that can be found in the LICENSE file.
4	
5	package domain
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9	
10		"github.com/bborbe/collection"
11		"github.com/bborbe/errors"
12		"github.com/bborbe/validation"
13	)
14	
15	// TaskPhase represents a phase in a task's lifecycle.
16	type TaskPhase string
17	
18	const (
19		// TaskPhaseTodo means the task is ready to start but needs planning.
20		TaskPhaseTodo TaskPhase = "todo"
21		// TaskPhasePlanning means the approach is being designed.
22		TaskPhasePlanning TaskPhase = "planning"
23		// TaskPhaseExecution means active implementation is underway.
24		// This is the canonical value; "in_progress" is accepted as an alias via NormalizeTaskPhase.
25		TaskPhaseExecution TaskPhase = "execution"
26		// TaskPhaseInProgress is an alias for TaskPhaseExecution kept for backward compatibility.
27		// Existing vault files with phase: "in_progress" continue to read and validate via NormalizeTaskPhase.
28		// Do not use TaskPhaseInProgress for new writes — use TaskPhaseExecution.
29		TaskPhaseInProgress TaskPhase = "in_progress"
30		// TaskPhaseAIReview means automated checks are running.
31		TaskPhaseAIReview TaskPhase = "ai_review"
32		// TaskPhaseHumanReview means manual review is required.
33		TaskPhaseHumanReview TaskPhase = "human_review"
34		// TaskPhaseDone means the task is ready to close.
35		TaskPhaseDone TaskPhase = "done"
36	)
37	
38	// AvailableTaskPhases lists all valid canonical task phase values.
39	var AvailableTaskPhases = TaskPhases{
40		TaskPhaseTodo,
41		TaskPhasePlanning,
42		TaskPhaseExecution,
43		TaskPhaseAIReview,
44		TaskPhaseHumanReview,
45		TaskPhaseDone,
46	}
47	
48	// TaskPhases is a collection of TaskPhase values.
49	type TaskPhases []TaskPhase
50	
51	// Contains returns true if the collection contains the given phase.
52	func (t TaskPhases) Contains(phase TaskPhase) bool {
53		return collection.Contains(t, phase)
54	}
55	
56	// String returns the string representation of the phase.
57	func (t TaskPhase) String() string {
58		return string(t)
59	}
60	
61	// Validate returns an error if the phase is not a valid canonical value.
62	func (t TaskPhase) Validate(ctx context.Context) error {
63		if !AvailableTaskPhases.Contains(t) {
64			return errors.Wrapf(ctx, validation.Error, "unknown task phase '%s'", t)
65		}
66		return nil
67	}
68	
69	// Ptr returns a pointer to a copy of the phase.
70	func (t TaskPhase) Ptr() *TaskPhase {
71		return &t
72	}
73	
74	// IsValidTaskPhase returns true if the phase is a valid canonical phase value.
75	func IsValidTaskPhase(phase TaskPhase) bool {
76		return AvailableTaskPhases.Contains(phase)
77	}
78	
79	// NormalizeTaskPhase converts alias phase values to their canonical form.
80	// Returns the canonical phase and true if valid, or empty and false if unknown.
81	func NormalizeTaskPhase(raw string) (TaskPhase, bool) {
82		// Check if already valid canonical phase
83		phase := TaskPhase(raw)
84		if IsValidTaskPhase(phase) {
85			return phase, true
86		}
87	
88		// Migration map for legacy/alias phase values
89		migrationMap := map[string]TaskPhase{
90			"in_progress": TaskPhaseExecution,
91		}
92	
93		if canonical, ok := migrationMap[raw]; ok {
94			return canonical, true
95		}
96	
97		return "", false
98	}

61	// truncateRunes returns s capped at max runes plus a trailing ellipsis. It

63	func truncateRunes(s string, max int) string {
64		if max < 0 {

163	func (a *application) Run(ctx context.Context, _ libsentry.Client) error {
164		registry := prometheus.NewRegistry()
165		jobMetrics := libmetrics.NewJobMetrics(registry, libtime.NewCurrentDateTime())
166		pusher := push.New(a.PushgatewayURL, libmetrics.BuildJobMetricsName(agentName)).
167			Grouping("agent", agentName).
168			Grouping("task_type", a.TaskType).
169			Collector(registry)
170		defer func() {
171			if err := pusher.PushContext(ctx); err != nil {
172				glog.Warningf("prometheus push failed: %v", err)
173				return
174			}
175			glog.V(2).Infof("prometheus push completed")
176		}()
177		start := libtime.NewCurrentDateTime().Now().Time()
178	
179		glog.V(2).Infof("github-dark-factory-agent started phase=%s", a.Phase)
180	
181		// Resolve the GitHub credential (App IAT or raw GH_TOKEN fallback) and make
182		// it usable by every git/gh subprocess. See prepareAuth.
183		resolvedToken, err := a.prepareAuth(ctx)
184		if err != nil {
185			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
186			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
187			return err
188		}
189	
190		deliverer := delivery.NewNoopResultDeliverer()
191		if a.TaskID != "" {
192			if len(a.KafkaBrokers) == 0 {
193				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
194				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
195				return errors.Errorf(ctx, "KAFKA_BROKERS must be set when TASK_ID is set")
196			}
197			syncProducer, err := factory.CreateSyncProducer(ctx, a.KafkaBrokers)
198			if err != nil {
199				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
200				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
201				return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "create sync producer")
202			}
203			defer func() {
204				if err := syncProducer.Close(); err != nil {
205					glog.Warningf("close sync producer failed: %v", err)
206				}
207			}()
208			deliverer = factory.CreateKafkaResultDeliverer(
209				syncProducer, a.TopicPrefix, a.TaskID, a.TaskContent,
210				libtime.NewCurrentDateTime(),
211			)
212		}
213	
214		claudeEnv := a.buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken)
215	
216		repoManager := factory.CreateRepoManager(a.ReposPath, a.WorkPath, resolvedToken)
217		githubClient := factory.CreateGitHubClient(resolvedToken)
218		claudeProber := factory.CreateClaudeProber(a.ClaudeConfigDir)
219		provider := factory.CreateAgentProvider(
220			a.ClaudeConfigDir,
221			a.AgentDir,
222			a.AnthropicModel,
223			resolvedToken,
224			claudeEnv,
225			repoManager,
226			githubClient,
227			claudeProber,
228			// Re-mint before the push: the installation token is minted once here at
229			// startup and expires after 60 minutes, but a lifecycle run routinely
230			// takes longer, so the final push would be refused as an invalid token.
231			a.resolveAuth,
232		)
233		agent, err := provider.Get(ctx, agentlib.TaskType(a.TaskType))
234		if err != nil {
235			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
236			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
237			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "select agent for task_type")
238		}
239	
240		result, err := agent.Run(ctx, a.Phase, a.TaskContent, deliverer)
241		if err != nil {
242			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
243			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
244			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "agent run failed")
245		}
246		jobMetrics.RecordRun(result.Status)
247		jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
248		return finishRun(ctx, result, a.Phase)
249	}
250	
251	// finishRun publishes the agent's result and then decides the Job's exit code.
252	// It exists as one call so Run stays within its funlen budget.
253	func finishRun(
254		ctx context.Context,
255		result *agentlib.Result,
256		phase domain.TaskPhase,
257	) error {
258		if err := agentlib.PrintResult(ctx, result); err != nil {
259			return err
260		}
261		return exitErrorForStatus(ctx, result.Status, phase, result.Message)
262	}
263	
264	// exitErrorForStatus returns a non-nil error when the agent's published status
265	// must fail the Job, and nil when the Job may exit 0.
266	//
267	// A failed result is still published to the task, but the Job must also exit
268	// non-zero. The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded
269	// in agent-task-executor's job_watcher), so returning nil here makes a failed run
270	// indistinguishable from a completed one: the failure is written as a phase
271	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at human_review
272	// as though a human had parked it deliberately (2026-11-03, task ceb79961: a Job
273	// that published Status=failed for a git clone error exited 0 and parked the
274	// task).
275	//
276	// needs_input is deliberately NOT a failure: parking for a human answer is that
277	// status's intent, and it reaches the same park path on purpose.
278	func exitErrorForStatus(
279		ctx context.Context,
280		status agentlib.AgentStatus,
281		phase domain.TaskPhase,
282		message string,
283	) error {
284		if status != agentlib.AgentStatusFailed {
285			return nil
286		}
287		displayMessage := truncateRunes(message, statusMessageMaxRunes)
288		if displayMessage == "" {
289			displayMessage = "(no message)"
290		}
291		err := errors.Errorf(
292			ctx,
293			"agent reported status %q for phase %q: %s",
294			status,
295			phase,
296			displayMessage,
297		)
298		return &statusError{
299			err: err,
300			fingerprint: []string{
301				"agent-status-failed",
302				string(phase),
303				causePrefix(message),
304			},
305		}
306	}
307	
308	// fingerprinter is implemented by errors that know their Sentry grouping key.
309	type fingerprinter interface {
310		Fingerprint() []string
311	}
312	
313	// statusError is the non-zero-exit error for a failed agent result. The
314	// capture-site stack is identical for every failure, so Sentry would merge
315	// unrelated planning / execution / ai_review causes into one issue; this type
316	// carries an explicit fingerprint (phase + bounded cause prefix) that
317	// sentryFingerprintProcessor installs on the event.
318	type statusError struct {
319		err         error
320		fingerprint []string
321	}
322	
323	func (e *statusError) Error() string { return e.err.Error() }
324	
325	// Unwrap keeps errors.Is / errors.As working through the wrapper.
326	func (e *statusError) Unwrap() error { return e.err }
327	
328	// Cause keeps github.com/bborbe/errors DataFromError traversal working.
329	func (e *statusError) Cause() error { return e.err }
330	
331	// Fingerprint is the Sentry grouping key for this failure.
332	func (e *statusError) Fingerprint() []string { return e.fingerprint }
333	
334	// sentryFingerprintProcessor installs the fingerprint carried by a
335	// fingerprinter error onto the Sentry event. It is a no-op for every other
336	// error, so it can be registered globally: service.Main owns the Sentry client
337	// and exposes no per-client event-processor hook.
338	func sentryFingerprintProcessor(
339		event *sentry.Event,
340		hint *sentry.EventHint,
341	) *sentry.Event {
342		if event == nil || hint == nil || hint.OriginalException == nil {
343			return event
344		}
345		var f fingerprinter
346		if errors.As(hint.OriginalException, &f) {
347			event.Fingerprint = f.Fingerprint()
348		}
349		return event
350	}
351	
352	// buildClaudeEnv assembles the Claude CLI subprocess env from the raw env
353	// pairs plus the Anthropic provider-routing overrides. resolvedToken, when
354	// non-empty, is threaded in as GH_TOKEN — the ai_review phase's Claude
355	// subprocess shells `gh pr view/diff`, and the runner strips pod env to an
356	// allowlist, so the token must be passed explicitly (os.Setenv in prepareAuth
357	// covers the dark-factory daemon path, not the Claude runner).
358	func (a *application) buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken string) map[string]string {
359		claudeEnv := envparse.KeyValuePairs(a.ClaudeEnvRaw)

361			claudeEnv = map[string]string{}
362		}
363		if a.AnthropicBaseURL != "" {

365		}
366		if a.AnthropicAuthToken != "" {
367			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"] = a.AnthropicAuthToken

22	
23	// TestExitErrorForStatus guards the exit-code contract between this agent and
24	// the executor that watches its Job.
25	//
26	// The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded in
27	// agent-task-executor's job_watcher) and never reads the Status this agent
28	// publishes. So a run that reports failure but exits 0 is written as a phase
29	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at
30	// human_review as though a human had parked it deliberately.
31	//
32	// Observed 2026-11-03: task ceb79961 published Status=failed for
33	// "git clone --bare: Failed to connect to github.com port 443", exited 0, and
34	// parked at human_review.
35	func TestExitErrorForStatus(t *testing.T) {
36		ctx := context.Background()
37		phase := domain.TaskPhase("execution")
38	
39		cases := []struct {
40			name    string
41			status  agentlib.AgentStatus
42			message string
43			wantErr bool
44		}{
45			{
46				name:    "failed must fail the Job so the executor does not record a phase success",
47				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusFailed,
48				message: "execution: ensure worktree: clone boom",
49				wantErr: true,
50			},
51			{
52				name:    "done exits 0",
53				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusDone,
54				wantErr: false,
55			},
56			{
57				name:    "in_progress exits 0",
58				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusInProgress,
59				wantErr: false,
60			},
61			{
62				// needs_input reaches the same park path on purpose: the task is meant
63				// to wait at human_review for an answer, not to be re-driven.
64				name:    "needs_input exits 0 — parking for a human answer is its intent",
65				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusNeedsInput,
66				wantErr: false,
67			},
68		}
69	
70		for _, c := range cases {
71			t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
72				err := exitErrorForStatus(ctx, c.status, phase, c.message)
73				if c.wantErr && err == nil {
74					t.Fatalf(
75						"status %q: expected a non-nil error, got nil — the Job would exit 0 and the executor would record it as a phase success",
76						c.status,
77					)
78				}
79				if !c.wantErr && err != nil {
80					t.Fatalf("status %q: expected nil, got %v", c.status, err)
81				}
82				if c.wantErr && !strings.Contains(err.Error(), c.message) {
83					t.Fatalf(
84						"failed error must include Result.Message %q, got %q",
85						c.message,
86						err.Error(),
87					)
88				}
89			})
90		}
91	}
92	
93	func TestExitErrorForStatusTruncatesLongMessage(t *testing.T) {
94		ctx := context.Background()
95		message := strings.Repeat("a", statusMessageMaxRunes+100)
96	
97		err := exitErrorForStatus(
98			ctx,
99			agentlib.AgentStatusFailed,
100			domain.TaskPhase("ai_review"),
101			message,
102		)
103		if err == nil {
104			t.Fatal("expected an error")
105		}
106		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), strings.Repeat("a", statusMessageMaxRunes)+"...") {
107			t.Fatalf(
108				"want the message truncated at %d runes with an ellipsis, got %q",
109				statusMessageMaxRunes,
110				err.Error(),
111			)
112		}
113		if strings.Contains(err.Error(), strings.Repeat("a", statusMessageMaxRunes+1)) {
114			t.Fatalf("message was not truncated: %q", err.Error())
115		}
116	}

118	func TestStatusErrorFingerprint(t *testing.T) {
119		ctx := context.Background()
120	
121		err := exitErrorForStatus(
122			ctx,
123			agentlib.AgentStatusFailed,
124			domain.TaskPhase("execution"),
125			"execution: ensure worktree: clone boom",
126		)
127		if err == nil {
128			t.Fatal("expected an error")
129		}
130	
131		var f fingerprinter
132		if !errors.As(err, &f) {
133			t.Fatalf("expected a fingerprinter error, got %T", err)
134		}
135		want := []string{
136			"agent-status-failed",
137			"execution",
138			"execution: ensure worktree: clone boom",
139		}
140		if !slices.Equal(f.Fingerprint(), want) {
141			t.Fatalf("fingerprint = %v, want %v", f.Fingerprint(), want)
142		}
143	}

145	func TestSentryFingerprintProcessor(t *testing.T) {
146		ctx := context.Background()
147	
148		t.Run("sets the fingerprint from a status error", func(t *testing.T) {
149			err := exitErrorForStatus(
150				ctx,
151				agentlib.AgentStatusFailed,
152				domain.TaskPhase("planning"),
153				"planning: PR #7 is not a draft",
154			)
155			event := &sentry.Event{}
156			got := sentryFingerprintProcessor(
157				event,
158				&sentry.EventHint{OriginalException: err},
159			)
160			want := []string{
161				"agent-status-failed",
162				"planning",
163				"planning: PR #7 is not a draft",
164			}
165			if !slices.Equal(got.Fingerprint, want) {
166				t.Fatalf("fingerprint = %v, want %v", got.Fingerprint, want)
167			}
168		})
169	
170		t.Run("leaves an unrelated error without a fingerprint", func(t *testing.T) {
171			event := &sentry.Event{}
172			got := sentryFingerprintProcessor(
173				event,
174				&sentry.EventHint{OriginalException: errors.New("boom")},
175			)
176			if len(got.Fingerprint) != 0 {
177				t.Fatalf("unexpected fingerprint %v", got.Fingerprint)
178			}
179		})
180	
181		t.Run("nil event and hint are safe", func(t *testing.T) {
182			if got := sentryFingerprintProcessor(nil, nil); got != nil {
183				t.Fatalf("expected nil event, got %v", got)
184			}
185		})
186	}

188	// TestPrintRedactsAnthropicAuthToken guards the startup argument dump against
189	// republishing the ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN value into the Job log.
190	//
191	// argument.Print honours only display:"hidden" and display:"length"; every other
192	// tag value falls through to the plaintext branch (`Argument: %s '%v'`). The root
193	// binary's application struct carried display:"password" — a value the printer does
194	// not implement — so each Job start wrote the live model-router credential in
195	// cleartext. This test drives the real printer over the real struct, so removing
196	// the display:"length" tag turns it red.
197	//
198	// Plain testing rather than Ginkgo on purpose: application is unexported, so the
199	// assertion must live in package main, and package main_test (main_test.go) shares
200	// this test binary — where a second RunSpecs fails with "calling RunSpecs more than
201	// once". An internal spec therefore cannot join the existing suite. Same shape as
202	// TestExitErrorForStatus above.
203	func TestPrintRedactsAnthropicAuthToken(t *testing.T) {
204		const sentinel = "sentinel-token-do-not-log-9f3a2b7c1d"
205	
206		var buf bytes.Buffer
207		log.SetOutput(&buf)
208		log.SetFlags(0)
209		defer func() {
210			log.SetOutput(os.Stderr)
211			log.SetFlags(log.LstdFlags)
212		}()
213	
214		if err := argument.Print(context.Background(), &application{AnthropicAuthToken: sentinel}); err != nil {
215			t.Fatalf("print: %v", err)
216		}
217	
218		rendered := buf.String()
219		if got := strings.Count(rendered, sentinel); got != 0 {
220			t.Fatalf(
221				"token value leaked into the argument dump: sentinel appeared %d times\n%s",
222				got,
223				rendered,
224			)
225		}
226		if got := strings.Count(rendered, "AnthropicAuthToken"); got != 1 {
227			t.Fatalf("want the field named exactly once, got %d\n%s", got, rendered)
228		}
229		if !strings.Contains(rendered, "Argument: AnthropicAuthToken length ") {
230			t.Fatalf("want the length form, got:\n%s", rendered)
231		}
232	}

18	
19	## Recommended Fix
20	
21	In finishRun, attach result.Message (truncated), task_id, task_type and phase to ctx via errors.AddToContext before exitErrorForStatus returns, so Sentry tags carry the cause without changing grouping; optionally exclude expected business-rule planning failures via a service.OptionsFn ExcludeErrors predicate while keeping the non-zero exit.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## Unreleased

- fix: **carry the failed result's message into the non-zero-exit error and fingerprint the Sentry event by phase + cause prefix.** `exitErrorForStatus` built its error from status and phase only, so every failed run produced the same capture-site stack and Sentry merged unrelated planning / execution / ai_review causes into one umbrella issue (`NUKE-PROD-CV`). The error now includes a 500-rune-bounded `Result.Message`, and a global Sentry event processor sets `event.Fingerprint` to `["agent-status-failed", <phase>, <first-line cause prefix, 100 runes>]`. The non-zero exit for `failed` is unchanged, and `needs_input` still exits 0 because parking for a human answer is its intent. Paging policy is deliberately unchanged
- chore: update Go to 1.27.4 (go.mod + Dockerfile) — clears `GO-2026-6859` (stdlib `net/http` `MaxBytesReader` header race), which the `vulncheck` gate reports at 1.27.3

## v0.6.2

- fix: link the pinned dark-factory clone to `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/dark-factory` so the authoring-rule paths the agents hardcode resolve — a local-path `marketplace add` never creates that directory, so prompt generation ran with no guides

## v0.6.1

- chore: restate the `do-not-merge` gate message to name its bypass actors — the Admin repository role and Integration `3907226`, both `bypass_mode: always` in the `master-protection` ruleset — instead of asserting an unqualified block

## v0.6.0

- feat: **build the release image on a cluster (`BUILD_TARGET=sun`), not only locally.** `make build` had a single arm — a local `docker build` — so publishing a release required a Docker daemon and `docker push` on the workstation. An agent is refused `docker push`, which made a release image unpublishable without a human at the keyboard. `Makefile.docker` now carries two arms, ported from `bborbe/a2a-worker-controller` and `bborbe/agent-claude`: `BUILD_TARGET=local` (the default, unchanged behaviour) and any other value, which renders `hack/build-job.yaml` as a Job on that cluster and pushes from inside it. The vendored `hack/` set is `a2a-worker-controller`'s hardened copy — templated namespace, `case`-based value whitelisting, no service-account token — rather than `agent-claude`'s older one. The cluster arm refuses to run without an explicit `VERSION` (the Makefile default is the newest release tag, so a defaulted build would overwrite a published image with one built from a different commit) and refuses to push a `vX.Y.Z` tag from any `REF` other than that tag. `upload` and `clean` are guarded so a remote build does not fail at a push step for an image that was never local. `Dockerfile` gains a `go mod vendor` step in its build stage: the local arm got `vendor/` from `check-go-mod`, but the cluster arm clones a git ref where `vendor/` is gitignored, so `-mod=vendor` would have failed there. `make precommit` now runs `shellcheck -S warning` over `hack/*.sh`, since those scripts handle the teamvault→Secret credential path

## v0.5.14

- fix: **redact the `AnthropicAuthToken` value from the startup argument dump.** The root binary's `application` struct carried `display:"password"` — a tag the argument printer does not implement. It honours only `display:"hidden"` and `display:"length"`, so every other value fell through to the plaintext branch (`Argument: %s '%v'`) and each Job start wrote the live model-router credential in cleartext into the cluster Job log. The field now carries `display:"length"`, matching the sibling in `cmd/run-task`, so the dump names the key and its length and never the value. A regression spec drives the real printer over the real struct and fails if the redaction is removed

## v0.5.13

- test: **cover the per-prompt setup fetch, not only the push.** `v0.5.12` moved the credential to a file-backed git helper, but only the push site had a regression spec — the fetch site (the one that failed first on 2026-11-03) was pinned by nothing. The new spec starts with token `A`, lets the lifecycle refresher mint `B`, and asserts the credential `git credential fill` resolves *during* the run is `B` — the A→B shape a "file is non-empty" check would not discriminate. No production code changes

## v0.5.12

- fix: **install a file-backed git credential helper so a long lifecycle run never uses an expired token.** The GitHub App installation token lives 60 minutes and is minted once at startup; `gh auth setup-git` binds it into a helper that resolves `GH_TOKEN` from the environment of whatever runs git, and the dark-factory daemon captured that environment when it was started — so no refresh in the parent process can reach it. A token file has no such lifetime: git re-reads it at every credential lookup. Observed 2026-11-03 on `bborbe/trading#433`: token minted 18:10Z, the daemon's own `git fetch origin` refused at 19:15Z with `Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported`

## v0.5.11

- fix: **exit non-zero when the agent publishes `Status: failed`.** The result was still published to the task, but the process returned nil, so the Job completed and the executor — which records a phase success on exit 0 alone (`IsJobSucceeded` in `agent-task-executor`'s `job_watcher`) and never reads the published Status — wrote a *phase success* for a run that had failed. Once the success grace expired the task was parked at `human_review` as though a human had parked it deliberately. Observed 2026-11-03 on task `ceb79961`: a Job that published `Status: failed` for `git clone --bare: Failed to connect to github.com port 443` exited 0 and parked the task. `needs_input` is deliberately unchanged — parking for a human answer is that status's intent

# github-dark-factory-agent — design.md

Design artifact for the Phase-2 gate of [[Lift Dark-Factory Daemon into Agent Framework]]. Produced via `/agent:launch-agent` (which walks the [[Agent Design Guide]] interview) on 2026-07-12, drawing on the Phase-1 prototype E2E (both slash-command prototypes validated on `bborbe/go-skeleton` PR #37 through merge).

## Part 1 — Motivation

- **Problem:** dark-factory's spec→prompt→execute lifecycle runs locally (`/dark-factory:daemon` / `run`), tying autonomous coding to one author + one awake laptop.
- **Do-nothing cost:** throughput capped at one author × one machine; no laptop-free execution.
- **This agent:** the cluster implementer. A human drafts + approves a spec on a draft-PR branch and walks away; this agent implements it and lands the task at `human_review`; the human verifies + flips the PR to ready; the existing `github-pr-review-agent` reviews + merges. Two human bookends, autonomous middle.

## Part 2 — Identity

- **Name / repo:** `github-dark-factory-agent` → `github.com/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent` (matches `github-pr-review-agent`, `github-releaser-agent` post-split convention). Image `docker.io/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent`.
- **Assignee (Config CRD `spec.assignee`):** `github-dark-factory-agent` — MUST match the `assignee` the watcher emits.
- **Pattern:** B (k8s Job per task). **Shape:** claude (mirrors `github-pr-review-agent`).
- **Runtime:** the Job pod IS a claude-yolo container (claude + git + gh + dark-factory CLI baked in).

## Part 3 — Integration

- **Trigger:** `github-dark-factory-watcher` (Phase-1: `/github-dark-factory-watcher` slash command; Phase-3: Go watcher). Emits when a draft PR has `.dark-factory.yaml` + ≥1 `approved`-not-`completed` spec **that appears in the PR's own diff** (diff-scoping — validated fix; "spec exists on branch" alone false-triggers on repos that persist specs).
- **Task contract:** [[Agent Task File Contract]] — `task_type: dark-factory-implement`, `assignee: github-dark-factory-agent`, `repo`/`clone_url`/`ref`/`pr_number`/`branch`; body is an operator-readable header, the clone is the data source.
- **Downstream:** lands task at `phase: human_review` (never flips the PR). Human flips draft→ready → `github-pr-watcher` → `github-pr-review-agent`.

## Part 4 — Behavior (phases)

| Phase | Impl shape | Reads | Side effects | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| planning | pure-Go spec scan (`agent/code` shape) | frontmatter (`clone_url`,`ref`,`branch`,`pr_number`) | clone branch, precondition checks (ref==HEAD, `.dark-factory.yaml`, approved-not-completed spec, PR draft) | `## Plan` |
| execution | custom step (dark-factory lifecycle + git) | `## Plan` | generate prompts → audit+approve → execute → verify → `spec complete`; commit + push per prompt | `## Result` |
| ai_review | `claudelib.NewAgentStep` (read-only) | `## Plan`+`## Result` | remote checks: all specs `completed`, no prompts in-flight, PR still draft, diff-vs-spec sanity | `## Review`; `phase: human_review`, clear assignee |

**Never runs `gh pr ready`.** The human's flip is the verification sign-off.

## Part 4.2 — ✅ Execution engine dependency (RESOLVED — shipped + live-validated)

The Phase-1 E2E surfaced a hard requirement: **dark-factory spawned nested claude-yolo containers** for the LLM steps. Since this agent's Job pod is *already* a claude-yolo container, that is DinD — disallowed (goal Non-goal).

**Prerequisite SHIPPED (2026-07-13): dark-factory `backend: local`** — a second `pkg/executor.Executor` (`localSubprocessExecutor`) that runs `claude` directly in the current process/cwd instead of `docker run`. Selected via config or `dark-factory run --set backend=local`. Git orchestration stays in the binary unchanged. Landed as spec 104, released **v0.192.0** (docs v0.192.1, scenario 024 v0.192.2). The agent's Dockerfile pins `DARK_FACTORY_VERSION=v0.192.0`.

**Live-validated 2026-07-13** with a real `dark-factory run --set`-style config (`backend: local`, `workflow: direct`, bare-remote sandbox):
- **Happy path:** a real approved prompt → claude ran **in-process (~11s), zero docker containers** → produced the change → `git commit` → prompt `completed`. This is the exact loop the execution step drives.
- **Fail path:** claude absent → fails closed (`claude not found on PATH`), no docker (scenario 024, `active`).

So the agent invokes `dark-factory run` (or per-prompt equivalents) with `--set backend=local` and lets dark-factory's Go binary do git; no nested containers, no DinD.

## Part 5 — Data contract & invariants

- Config via `--set` at runtime, NEVER committed to the PR branch (committed `.dark-factory.yaml` divergence conflicts `workflow:direct`'s `git merge origin/master`). Keep the branch current with `origin/<default>`.
- **★ claude auth is HOME-sensitive (live-smoke finding 2026-07-13).** `backend: local` runs `claude` as a subprocess inheriting the pod's env. If `claude`'s login credential is not discoverable from the process's `HOME`, every prompt fails fast with `Not logged in · Please run /login` (observed: overriding `HOME` broke auth even with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set). **Requirement:** the Job pod MUST provision claude's login where the agent process's `HOME` resolves it — bake/mount the credential into the runtime `HOME` (claude-yolo image convention), do NOT rely on `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` alone. Add a startup precondition check: run a trivial `claude --print` (or reuse dark-factory's claude probe) and fail the task early with a clear escalation if unauthed, rather than failing every prompt.
- **★ the dark-factory Claude PLUGIN must be installed, not just the CLI (E2E root cause 2026-07-13).** backend:local's generation and prompt-audit steps run the slash commands `/dark-factory:generate-prompts-for-spec` and `/dark-factory:audit-prompt` *inside* claude. If the runtime `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` has the CLI binary but not the plugin, claude reports `Unknown command: /dark-factory:generate-prompts-for-spec` → **zero prompts generated → the spec resets to `approved` and the daemon idles at "nothing to do"** (silent — no error surfaces to the agent; looks like a generation-trigger bug but is really a provisioning gap). **Requirement:** the Dockerfile installs the plugin at build time (`claude plugin marketplace add bborbe/dark-factory && claude plugin install dark-factory@dark-factory`, verified with `claude plugin list | grep -q dark-factory`), mirroring github-pr-review-agent's build-time `coding` install. Keep the plugin's minor aligned with `DARK_FACTORY_VERSION`.
- **★ backend:local ignores dark-factory `config.env` (spec-104 gap).** `pkg/executor.localSubprocessExecutor.buildCommand` passes `--model` from config but never sets `cmd.Env` — so the subprocess inherits only the *ambient* process env. Unlike the docker backend (which injects `config.env` into the container), backend:local does NOT apply `env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` / token from `~/.config/dark-factory/config.yaml`. **Requirement:** the Job pod sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (model router) and the auth token as **pod env vars**, not via dark-factory `config.env`. (Follow-up: dark-factory could merge `config.env` into the local subprocess env so one config works for both backends.)
- Agent MUST drive `dark-factory spec complete` (else spec stays `verifying` = approved-not-completed → watcher re-emits).
- Idempotency: `AgentStep.ShouldRun` checks if the phase's `##` section exists; per-prompt commits make execution crash-resumable.
- Concurrency: per-repo cap 1 (Config CRD) — two PRs on one repo must not race git push.

## Part 6 — Operations

- Pattern B Job (not cron); resource profile ~ `github-pr-review-agent`.
- Kill switch: remove/disable the Config CRD.
- Observability: phase-transition logs + metrics; per-prompt execution visible.

## Part 7 — Safety / failure modes

1. **Prompt fails DoD / audit fail** — spec-078 fail-closed stops the spec; agent escalates (clear assignee, `previous_assignee`, phase unchanged). NO auto-fix loop.
2. **Spec has no scenario** — `verify-spec` can't pass; either require a scenario at watcher-emit time, or `spec complete` after prompts (less safety). Decide at build time.
3. **`workflow:direct` git-merge-origin/master conflict** — mitigated by config-via-`--set` + non-divergent branch + pre-run sync.
4. Security: GH token + git-push creds via Secret; PR content visible to claude (acceptable, zero-retention).

### Auto-approve blast radius (accepted)

The execution phase runs dark-factory with `--auto-approve-prompts`. This is the intended bookend design, not a blind approval. The flag triggers dark-factory's spec-078 audit-then-approve: each auto-generated prompt is AUDITED headlessly and approved only if the audit passes (fail-closed — a failing audit stops the spec and the agent escalates). The blast radius is bounded by four independent gates: (a) the human pre-approves the SPEC on the draft PR before the agent runs (first bookend); (b) the spec-078 fail-closed audit gate on every generated prompt; (c) this agent's ai_review diff-vs-spec sanity check before `human_review`; (d) the human's draft→ready flip on the PR (final bookend). The execution pod is single-tenant and ephemeral, so a rogue prompt cannot reach beyond the one PR branch. dark-factory has no per-prompt-id allowlist (`--auto-approve-prompt-ids` does not exist) — the audit gate IS the allowlist.

## Part 8 — Acceptance (per goal SCs)

Deployed in dev, consumes a real watcher task, walks planning→execution→ai_review in one pod, lands at `human_review` without flipping the PR; output parity with the Phase-1 prototype; idempotent under replay; per-repo concurrency 1. ✅ Prerequisite (dark-factory `backend: local`) shipped v0.192.0 and live-validated — the build is unblocked.

## Open decisions

1. ~~Execution engine: build the dark-factory local Executor first~~ — **RESOLVED**: built + shipped as `backend: local` (v0.192.0), live-validated happy + fail paths. The agent drives `dark-factory run --set backend=local`.
2. Scenario-required-or-not for verify (Part 7.2). Leaning: do NOT hard-require a scenario at emit time (spec 104 itself shipped without one, verified by unit tests + the live-smoke); instead the agent runs `spec complete` after prompts pass DoD, and `verify-spec` when a scenario exists. Revisit once the watcher emits real tasks.

package domain

import (
	"context"

	"github.com/bborbe/collection"
	"github.com/bborbe/errors"
	"github.com/bborbe/validation"
)

// TaskPhase represents a phase in a task's lifecycle.
type TaskPhase string

const (
	// TaskPhaseTodo means the task is ready to start but needs planning.
	TaskPhaseTodo TaskPhase = "todo"
	// TaskPhasePlanning means the approach is being designed.
	TaskPhasePlanning TaskPhase = "planning"
	// TaskPhaseExecution means active implementation is underway.
	// This is the canonical value; "in_progress" is accepted as an alias via NormalizeTaskPhase.
	TaskPhaseExecution TaskPhase = "execution"
	// TaskPhaseInProgress is an alias for TaskPhaseExecution kept for backward compatibility.
	// Existing vault files with phase: "in_progress" continue to read and validate via NormalizeTaskPhase.
	// Do not use TaskPhaseInProgress for new writes — use TaskPhaseExecution.
	TaskPhaseInProgress TaskPhase = "in_progress"
	// TaskPhaseAIReview means automated checks are running.
	TaskPhaseAIReview TaskPhase = "ai_review"
	// TaskPhaseHumanReview means manual review is required.
	TaskPhaseHumanReview TaskPhase = "human_review"
	// TaskPhaseDone means the task is ready to close.
	TaskPhaseDone TaskPhase = "done"
)

// AvailableTaskPhases lists all valid canonical task phase values.
var AvailableTaskPhases = TaskPhases{
	TaskPhaseTodo,
	TaskPhasePlanning,
	TaskPhaseExecution,
	TaskPhaseAIReview,
	TaskPhaseHumanReview,
	TaskPhaseDone,
}

// TaskPhases is a collection of TaskPhase values.
type TaskPhases []TaskPhase

// Contains returns true if the collection contains the given phase.
func (t TaskPhases) Contains(phase TaskPhase) bool {
	return collection.Contains(t, phase)
}

// String returns the string representation of the phase.
func (t TaskPhase) String() string {
	return string(t)
}

// Validate returns an error if the phase is not a valid canonical value.
func (t TaskPhase) Validate(ctx context.Context) error {
	if !AvailableTaskPhases.Contains(t) {
		return errors.Wrapf(ctx, validation.Error, "unknown task phase '%s'", t)
	}
	return nil
}

// Ptr returns a pointer to a copy of the phase.
func (t TaskPhase) Ptr() *TaskPhase {

=== definition-of-done.md ===
# Definition of Done — Dark Factory Prompts

Rules that every dark-factory prompt execution must satisfy before reporting success.

## Test Coverage

**New code** (new files, new packages):
- Aim for ≥80% statement coverage
- Test all public functions
- Test error paths and edge cases (empty input, nil, invalid values)

**Modified code** (changes to existing files):
- Test all changed/added code paths — every new branch, every new condition
- Existing untested code does NOT need retroactive coverage
- If adding a new field/method to a struct, test the new behavior

**Verification (Go):**
```bash
go test -coverprofile=/tmp/cover.out -mod=vendor ./affected/pkg/...
go tool cover -func=/tmp/cover.out | grep "changed_file"
```

**Verification (Python):**
```bash
pytest --cov=affected_module --cov-report=term-missing
```

## Code Quality

- Follow project CLAUDE.md conventions
- Follow all relevant docs in `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/coding/docs/`
- This includes ALL guides (Go, Python, shell, documentation, etc.) — not just language-specific ones
- Self-review diff against the checklist in CLAUDE.md before `make precommit`

## Verification

- `make test` after each meaningful change (fast feedback)
- `make precommit` once at the end (full validation)
- **Multi-service repos:** only run in the changed service directory, never at repo root
- **YAML/config-only changes:** skip `make precommit`, use the prompt's `<verification>` commands
- Non-zero exit code from `make precommit` = failed, no exceptions

## Changelog

- Update `CHANGELOG.md` with `## Unreleased` entry if project has one
- See `changelog-guide.md` for format rules

## Completion

- Report honest status: success only if `make precommit` exit code 0
- Include verification command and exit code in report
=== changelog-guide (head 60) ===
---
tags:
  - guide
  - git
  - documentation
---

Guide for writing consistent, useful CHANGELOG.md entries in dark-factory projects.

## Goal

Produce changelog entries with conventional prefixes so dark-factory can determine the version bump automatically — no guessing from prose.

## File Structure

```markdown
# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

Please choose versions by [Semantic Versioning](http://semver.org/).

* MAJOR version when you make incompatible API changes,
* MINOR version when you add functionality in a backwards-compatible manner, and
* PATCH version when you make backwards-compatible bug fixes.

## Unreleased

- feat: Add SpecWatcher to monitor specs/ for approved status changes
- fix: Remove stale Docker container before starting a new executor run

## v1.5.0

- feat: Add FuncRunner interface for executing functions with custom behavior
- fix: Fix WaiterUntil to handle equal times correctly
```

### RULE changelog/preamble-frozen (MUST)

**Owner**: agent-auditor
**Applies when**: a CHANGELOG.md edit inserts content above the `# Changelog` title, modifies the SemVer preamble bullets (MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH), or places a `## Unreleased` / `## vX.Y.Z` section inside (rather than after) the preamble block.
**Enforcement**: `scripts/rule-checks.sh` (checks `# Changelog` is first content; flags any `## Unreleased`/`## vX.Y.Z` before the preamble block)
**Why**: The preamble is the API contract between the changelog and every tool that parses it (dark-factory's version-bump detector, /coding:commit's CHANGELOG validator, downstream release-notes generators). Moving / deleting / shifting it breaks the parsers silently — the next release attempt either bumps the wrong version or misses entries entirely. Restoring is cheap; preventing the edit is cheaper.

#### Bad

```markdown
## Unreleased
- feat: new thing

# Changelog                          ← preamble shoved below
All notable changes...
```

#### Good

```markdown
# Changelog
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
Please choose versions by [Semantic Versioning](http://semver.org/).
